projects.name: Arcnode
projects.long: One Turborepo monorepo for the website, Backboard (the OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect account service every Arcnode app signs in with), the game API, the relay for Arcnode Remote, the status page and the community bot. Deployed on Vercel and Railway.
projects.description: My studio: projects, downloads, a client portal and the sign-in service behind every app.

case.problem: Every app I made needed the same things: an account, downloads, updates, a status page and somewhere to ask for help. Building those again inside each app would mean a separate login for every app and the same bugs fixed five times.
case.built: One monorepo that holds all of it. Backboard is my own OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect sign-in service with PKCE, so every app signs in with "Login with Arcnode". Next to it: the website with a client portal, a games API for profiles, leaderboards and cloud saves, a pipeline that signs game releases, a status page and the community bot.
case.result: ArcJournal, Arcnode Games and Arcnode Remote all sign in with one Arcnode account, and every game release is signed and checked before it runs. A new app starts with accounts, updates and support already there.

lines: # Arcnode
IMG0
### My studio: projects, downloads, a client portal and the sign-in service behind every app.
One Turborepo monorepo for the website, Backboard (the OAuth 2.0 and OpenID
Connect account service every Arcnode app signs in with), the game API, the
relay for Arcnode Remote, the status page and the community bot. Deployed on
Vercel and Railway.
Built with Next.js · Hono · PostgreSQL · Turborepo
## Case study
**The problem**
Every app I made needed the same things: an account, downloads, updates, a
status page and somewhere to ask for help. Building those again inside each
app would mean a separate login for every app and the same bugs fixed five
times.
**What I built**
One monorepo that holds all of it. Backboard is my own OAuth 2.0 and OpenID
Connect sign-in service with PKCE, so every app signs in with "Login with
Arcnode". Next to it: the website with a client portal, a games API for
profiles, leaderboards and cloud saves, a pipeline that signs game releases,
a status page and the community bot.
**The result**
ArcJournal, Arcnode Games and Arcnode Remote all sign in with one Arcnode
account, and every game release is signed and checked before it runs. A new
app starts with accounts, updates and support already there.
[Visit](https://arcnode.dev)

projects.name: Arcnode Remote
projects.long: Help anyone over the internet with a one-time code. The person at the computer sees who is helping (confirmed by Arcnode), compares a six-digit code and can disconnect at any moment. Sessions are end-to-end encrypted with Noise XX and go through the Arcnode relay over TLS 1.3. View only or full control, every screen at once, chat, file transfer and any-time access.
projects.description: Remote support for Windows, end-to-end encrypted, on the other person's terms.

case.problem: Remote-support apps are also what phone scammers ask people to install. Someone getting help should see exactly who is connecting, decide what that person may do and be able to stop it at any moment.
case.built: A Windows app in Tauri, Rust and React. The helper shares a nine-digit code that works once and expires after ten minutes. The other person sees the helper's Arcnode account, compares a six-digit code and approves every permission separately. Sessions are end-to-end encrypted with the Noise XX protocol and pass through a relay that cannot read them.
case.result: It can be downloaded from remote.arcnode.dev and installs signed updates. It is still in active development: so far I have tested it with both ends on one PC, and testing between separate computers is next.

projects.name: Rosa Wildlife Reserve
projects.long: rosarealism.com with a member dashboard, five Discord bots (applications, tickets, player progress, voice) and a desktop app for staff, all in one monorepo on a shared PostgreSQL database that talks to the game server, with tests and releases on GitHub.
projects.description: The website and five Discord bots behind a Path of Titans realism server.

case.problem: A hardcore realism server for Path of Titans, a multiplayer dinosaur survival game. Staff needed one place for applications, reports, penalties, appeals and tickets that also reached into the game itself, and members needed a home for their characters outside Discord.
case.built: Five Discord bots that each do one job, and rosarealism.com with a page for every member and character, all on one PostgreSQL database. The bots talk to the game server directly, so a ban decided in Discord is carried out in the game. A separate status page keeps working when everything else is down.
case.result: Live for a Discord of more than 2,700 members, with 177 bot commands. Staff run applications, reports and tickets with the game server in the loop, and change how the bots behave from the website without a new release.

projects.name: Bemmel & Kroon Scheduling
projects.long: An internal web app where staff, team leads and management handle rosters, absence and staff planning. It started in PHP and MySQL in 2025 and grew into a Next.js platform with Excel and calendar export, email notifications and an installable PWA. The screenshots use made-up names.
projects.description: Rosters, absence and staff planning for Bemmel & Kroon, with rights per role.

case.problem: Bemmel & Kroon sells kitchens and appliances online and in three showrooms. Planning shifts across departments and locations, with absence and leave in the same picture, was spread over separate tools.
case.built: An internal web app with a weekly roster grid and published snapshots, absence and leave inside the schedule, rights per role, location and department, an audit log and an analytics dashboard. It started in PHP and MySQL in 2025 and I rebuilt it in Next.js, with Excel and calendar export, email notifications and an installable app for phones.
case.result: One private app where staff, team leads and management plan shifts and handle absence, on a desktop or a phone, with a record of who changed what.

projects.name: Exit Only
projects.long: The police only know where you are while someone can see you: break every line of sight around corners, through traffic and under the Plaza Tunnel, and stay out of the helicopter searchlight until they give up. Crashes leave dents and glass on the road, the car drives with gears and real grip, and Rooftop Rush adds a sliding-vehicle puzzle on a gridlocked parking deck. Every car, building and sound is made in-house. Free on Arcnode Games.

projects.name: ArcJournal
projects.long: Write daily entries, tag the mood behind them and grade your days, so patterns show up in your stats. Version 2 encrypts every entry on your computer with AES-256-GCM before it is saved, with a key only your passphrase or recovery key can open. Signs in with Arcnode and updates itself on every platform.
